subject: Urgent: gen-api p95 spike / coordinated mitigation + customer comms
messages:
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] gen-api p95 spike seen 07:58-08:15 PST — immediate triage requested

Team —

Monitoring just opened an incident: gen-api p95 jumped from baseline ~210ms to ~2.4s in the 07:58–08:15 PST window. Errors are low, but tail latency for streaming and non-streaming gen endpoints spiked and correlated with:

- Increase in KV cache churn (cache miss rate +20% over baseline)
- A small subset of customers (top 10 tenants by QPS) showing >3x token amplification
- Node-level CPU on a handful of serving hosts at ~92% for sustained 10m slices

I've attached the windowed latency graph and the heap dump the ops agent captured for the most impacted host (prod-heapdump-20280419.tar.gz).

Immediate asks:
- Ben: can SRE confirm whether KV eviction TTLs changed or if there was a background job (snapshot/compaction) that lined up with this window? Any emergency mitigations you can trigger now (routing to warm pool, rolling drain, temporary QPS gating)?
- Marissa / Karthik: from product/serving side, can we consider an emergency toggle to fall back the affected route to quantized-1 model variant or reduce batching to prioritize latency? Need fast tradeoffs and what we will need post-mortem-wise.
- Jonas: please stand by for a short customer note we may push to Cartline — they are already seeing degraded UX and have asked for an ETA.

I'll stand up a short bridge in 5 if helpful (standup link: https://meet.redwood.com/bridge/inf-2179).

Chloe
Customer Ops / Incident Liaison
Redwood Inference

Attachments: latency-20280419-window.png, prod-heapdump-20280419.tar.gz

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] gen-api p95 spike seen 07:58-08:15 PST — immediate triage requested

On Thu, Apr 19, 2028 at 08:23 AM Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Monitoring just opened an incident: gen-api p95 jumped ...

Thanks Chloe — I’m on it. Quick notes from initial triage (on the bridge):

1) KV eviction spike: Confirmed. Redis miss rate jumped; eviction stats show a run of LRU evictions starting 07:50. No config changes in the last 24h. Likely workload-driven (sudden prefix fanout from a tenant).
2) Affected hosts: host-gw-12 and host-gw-15 show high kernel steal and short-lived GC pauses in the process. Uploaded heap dump looks like many ephemeral allocations from streaming sessions.
3) Immediate mitigations I’m enacting now (ETA ~3–7m):
   - Route 10% of traffic for top-affected tenant (Cartline) to dedicated warm pool (will reduce throughput capacity by ~8% for others while live).
   - Increase KV cache TTL for serving layer from 60s -> 300s for the next 20m (to reduce eviction churn).
   - Trigger rolling restart of host-gw-15 with graceful drain (will keep host-gw-12 for traffic).
4) Short-term fallback options (need product signoff): enable quantized-1 fallback route for non-streaming gen endpoints (trades ~5–8% quality for ~30–40% latency reduction).

I’ll paste quick commands on the bridge; I’ll also open INF-2179 with a triage checklist and capture each mitigation.

-Ben
Ben Carter
SRE — Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP-sla-variance-20280419.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [ALERT] gen-api p95 spike seen 07:58-08:15 PST — immediate triage requested

Thanks Ben — looks like reasonable stopgaps. A few product/engineering asks so we can make this deterministic and not brittle:

- Can SRE correlate whether the eviction pattern is tenant-scoped (single tenant fans) or global? If tenant-scoped, we should add per-tenant cache quotas and fail-open limits (short-term: per-tenant prefix cache cap).
- Karthik / Product: we need a product decision on fallback behavior. Options:
   1) Immediate canary: flip quantized-1 for non-streaming endpoints for Cartline only (route-level toggle).
   2) Broader conservative routing: reduce batch window from 100ms->40ms platform-wide for 30m.
   3) Operational: raise cache TTL (Ben is doing) + synthetic cache warmer for the affected tenant.

From roadmap perspective: we should accelerate the per-tenant cache quotas and a graceful degrade for streaming sessions (patch targeted for next sprint but we may bump). For today — I support (1) for Cartline canary + the cache TTL raise. Ben, please proceed and I’ll coordinate the canary toggle with infra/API layer.

Marissa
Eng Lead, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Pete Lyons <pete.lyons@cartline.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: degraded responses this morning — impact on Cartline

Pete —

Short update for leadership: we observed a transient increase in tail latency impacting a small subset of tenants, including Cartline. Our SRE team identified elevated KV cache eviction and CPU contention on a limited set of serving hosts and immediately enacted mitigations: routing affected traffic to a warm pool, increasing serving cache TTLs, and restarting one overloaded host.

What this means for Cartline:
- We have applied a tenant-specific traffic reroute that preserves request ordering and idempotency.
- We are rolling a temporary, conservative fallback for non-streaming generation (quality tradeoff ~5–8%) only if you prefer it; otherwise, we will keep your traffic on the warm pool and monitor.
- Expected timeline: stabilization in 10–25 minutes from now; we will confirm when p95 returns below 400ms and follow up with a post-mortem.

I’ll keep you posted in the next 10m.

Regards,
Chloe
Customer Ops / Incident Liaison
Redwood Inference

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Incident update: stabilization confirmed + next steps

Team —

Quick closure notes:
- p95 returned to ~320ms by 10:45 after the routing and TTL mitigations. No further errors recorded. Cartline confirmed UX improved.
- Actions completed:
  1) Tenant-specific reroute to warm pool (Ben) — complete
  2) KV cache TTL raised to 300s for 20m window (Ben) — complete
  3) Rolling restart of host-gw-15 (Ben) — complete
  4) Cartline canary decision: opted NOT to flip quantized fallback (Marissa/Karthik) — agreed to keep warm-pool approach

Follow-ups / owners:
- Ben: capture full eviction histogram + timeline in INF-2179 and include host-level metrics (due EOD today).
- Marissa: schedule an expedited spike on per-tenant cache quotas and a short PRD for graceful degrade on streaming (target: next sprint planning).
- Karthik: evaluate whether batch-window auto-shrink heuristic should be enabled for noisy tenants (POC by next week).
- Jonas: send the customer-facing post-incident note to Cartline once we have the finalized timeline and the post-mortem link (I’ll draft; please review).

Thanks all for the fast coordination. I’ll mark this thread as the incident liaison record and we’ll attach the post-mortem when available.

Chloe
Customer Ops / Incident Liaison
Redwood Inference
